_METHOD: Six tabs = six disciplines in sequence. PRE-CALL: orient before contact (True North, register/intent, intel, questions, landmines). EX-ANTE: file a decision receipt BEFORE the event (hypothesis + predicted Y-gate + pre-committed move + falsifier) so you can be scored later. FORGE: pressure-test the brief's own claims against external substrates via an independent skeptic (grounded / inference / struck). RECOIL: after the event, close the receipt — belief-update ledger (confidence x conviction), kairos/quiet-signals, risk flags, next steps. WAR GAME: adversarial + kinematic — measured manifold, BAR/LAB/COURT gauntlet, ATG pre-mortem on the critical path vs their real objections. DEFENSIBILITY: translate the method into the counterpart's native register (Rosetta) + a 5-verb x 4-proofing matrix + the antifragile-core / lossless-translation test.

header.title: Sara Hagey Chima · Concourse
header.sub: Recruiter screen Fri Oct 16; peer FDE call with Krish Mon Oct 19 (closed). Next: design take-home, then onsite. FDE track.

p: Take the FDE seat as the container for the whole blend, learn from the peer how the FDE/FDPM line really works, and keep level and comp for the hiring manager after the take-home.

rows.v: Take-home spec from Sara (design-focused), then onsite v0 build. Peer call with Krish done Mon Oct 19.
Recruiter screen and peer call done. Next readers: hiring manager and CTO via the take-home.
Get a qualified FDE into the pipe quickly. Sara said the full process can finish in two weeks or less.
YELLOW. Skills fit looks strong, but level, comp and in-person are unresolved.

blocks.intro: Concourse is a New York AI-native GovTech company. Most diagnostic facts first.

items.html: Pod model: about 90-day deployments, one FDE plus one FDPM. FDE owns most of the build, FDPM owns intake to delivery and is about 50% in Claude Code.
Load: 4 to 6 deployments at once per person. Sara: about 1 trip a month. A third-party listing says about 5 days per quarter, so ask which is right.
Process: peer call, take-home built in Claude Code within 72 hours (hiring manager reviews it), onsite. FDPM pivot adds a PM conversation.
Org: about 25 people, flat, everyone reports to the CEO, no formal levels. Moved to a Chelsea office on Oct 16. Five days a week in person.

Public record: onconcourse.com says more than 100 federal, state and local partners. A third-party FDE listing shows $170k to $220k plus equity, 1 to 5 years, about 25% client time and 75% building. Unverified on their own site.
Not this company: the Ashby board you linked (jobs.ashbyhq.com/concourse) belongs to a finance-AI Concourse. Do not use anything from it.

blocks.intro: For the Monday peer call. Ask to learn, not to negotiate.

items.html: Which deployments are you on now and how is your time split? · look for: real numbers, not a pitch.
Where does FDE end and FDPM begin in practice? Who writes the spec and who owns compliance? · look for: a concrete handoff, not 'we all do everything'.
Is the 25/75 client/build split real, and how much travel actually happens? · look for: whether it matches Sara's 'one trip a month'.
How much of the shared platform do FDEs own, and who dogfoods internal CI/CD and governance? · look for: an opening for the systems-engineering hat.
What does a strong take-home look like to the hiring manager? · look for: criteria you can design to.
Landmine: raising level or comp with the peer. They cannot decide it and it reads as a negotiation before the take-home.
Landmine: repeating the four-hat pitch. Sara already said it is the FDE role. Show it in the take-home instead.

INFERENCE = my read, not forced. STRUCK = overreach, corrected. No independent skeptic agent was run on this pass, so rulings are mine.

blocks.intro: Read from the transcript, not felt.

items.html: Kairos: Sara offered a faster process when Zach mentioned other things coming. The window to move quickly is open now and tied to his timeline.
Quiet signal: she asked for the take-home send time to be Zach's choice. That is a rare amount of control for a candidate.
Quiet signal: 'the goal' is to be competitive when comp was raised. She did not say yes to a number.
Risk: level. A posting built for 1 to 5 years and an org with no leveling means a senior ask has no existing slot.
Risk: five days a week in Chelsea from Connecticut. Zach said it depends on the team and office, which is not a yes.
Risk: the call audio broke up near the end. Take-home hours were asked twice and never answered.

blocks.h2: Receipt closed · Monday peer call (Krish) vs ex-ante

rows.v: FDEs do scoping, build, light pre-sales and platform contribution; FDPM mostly intake. Travel under one trip a month. YELLOW.

Build and platform: yes. Pre-sales: mostly no (FDPM, demo people and a growing AE team carry it). FDPM: intake, access and scope before the FDE joins. Travel: not discussed. Informal, easy call; Krish took Zach's email.
Partly fired. 'FDEs do not touch pre-sales' is true; 'platform owned by a separate team' is false (FDEs platformize in hypercare). The blend survives as build plus platform, minus GTM.
YELLOW, unchanged. Role content fits on build and platform; level, comp and in-person still open.
the really key piece of the FDE role is that platform product feedback loop.

blocks.intro: From the transcript and Zach's notes right after.

items.html: Scale: about 30 deployments live past hypercare; each FDE or FDPM carries 4 or 5 in flight. Muni and state work (Ohio agencies named).
Stack: TypeScript front and back, AWS, Postgres; defaults, not fixed. Prefer best-in-class (Stripe) unless the contract forces otherwise.
Pre-kickoff: an operations team clears access and data before the pod is staffed; parallel deployments absorb blockers.
Take-home clue 1: ambiguity is sometimes intentional; it mirrors the real environment. State assumptions.
Take-home clue 2: startup pace; the first version does not need to be perfect, it needs to exist.
Take-home format: design-focused spec, then onsite build of a v0. Questions go by email, or straight to Krish and the CTO (name heard as 'Rappolis'; spelling unconfirmed).
Quiet signal: Krish agreed with the now/next/later vendor-lock trade-off framing ('100%') and said explaining GovCloud vs public cloud trade-offs is a big part of the engineering piece.

Quiet signal: Zach shared concourse.arcs.care and invited Krish or the CTO to press on weak points and send clarifying questions; Krish said he would give it a pass and took Zach's email. Watch for questions back.
Risk: no open source now and no plans ('can often come with a fair few trade-offs'). The public-goods angle is not a wedge here.

Commit count, reconciled: both numbers are true. Main has 5,002 commits since 2026-04-09 counting merge commits (what Zach said on the call, 'almost 5,000 since April') and 3,551 without merges; status.arcs.care shows 3,575. Written materials keep 'over 3,500'; if it comes up, say 'about 3,500 commits, about 5,000 counting merges'.
Risk: long intro and an ARCS method explanation took much of the 30 minutes; the hiring manager will see the design, so keep the take-home tight.

blocks.intro: Adversarial pass on the opportunity, not the person.

items.html: BAR (ruin): spending weeks on a take-home and an onsite for a seat whose level and comp will not meet the target. Mitigation: get the comp conversation scheduled before the onsite, not after.

LAB · Loki: the flexibility language is the cheapest thing a recruiter can offer. Steel-manned down: it is a real signal in a 25-person flat company where the CEO can set a number, but it is not a number.
COURT: no claim about Concourse goes into the recruiter brief unless it traces to the transcript or their own site. Third-party figures stay out.

p: Being wrong early was the highest-information event of the day: the finance-AI assumption died in one web check, before it reached a recruiter or the peer call.

Lossless test: I will take on one deployment from scoping through delivery, reuse what I build for the next one, and help the team run its own tools the way it runs its customers'. If that holds in their words, with no ARCS vocabulary, it is defensible.
